title: Trout on toast with buttery grapes

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Crème fraîche, horseradish sauce, butter, trout, grapes, bread and watercress are all ordinary home staples or fresh foods.

supermarket.reason: Trout fillets, red grapes, watercress and crème fraîche are all everyday Tesco lines at normal prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a frying pan and a toaster or grill, and the technique is simple pan-frying.

works.reason: Four trout fillets fried skin side down for 4 minutes and turned for 1 is sound, and 200g grapes and 100g crème fraîche suit four slices of toast for four people.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes covers halving the grapes, snipping chives, mixing the sauce and toasting, and the 7 minutes matches the frying and warming in the steps.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including chives, lemon, salt and pepper, is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: Warm buttery grapes are named in the title and are a substantial topping rather than a garnish, which suits late October.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Oily fish on wholemeal toast with watercress and fruit is a proper, filling breakfast a family would happily eat again.
